language.script_notes: Filipino (Tagalog-based) and English, with Tagalog the dominant local language around Manila and Ilocano in the northwest — the region where Filipino is most heard in daily use.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Yellow-and-black striped concrete guardrails in the Cordillera mountains of the north; white guardrails with three recurring black stripes are unique to the Bicol region in southern Luzon.
road_furniture.curb_style: Dense formal infrastructure in Metro Manila with elevated expressways and rail.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: A pole-top made of two tall vertical L-shaped metal bars connected by thin wires, resembling a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area. Square concrete poles with an indent on both sides are mainly found north of Manila.

architecture.roof_style: Corrugated metal roofing dominates; nipa thatch on traditional bahay kubo houses in rural areas.
architecture.wall_construction: Dense concrete hollow-block construction in Metro Manila; Spanish colonial stone churches ('earthquake Baroque') and bahay na bato houses in old towns such as Vigan; Ifugao stilt houses and granaries in the northern mountains.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bare and painted grey concrete, layered with advertising signage.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Manila's dense high-rise and informal-settlement mix; Vigan's preserved Spanish colonial streets (UNESCO); the 2,000-year-old Ifugao rice terraces in Banaue and stilted Ifugao houses; Spanish colonial churches and jeepney-choked boulevards.

nature.vegetation: Rice paddies dominate the central Luzon plain; terraced rice fields and pine forest in the northern Cordillera highlands; coconut palms along coasts and southern Luzon.
nature.terrain: The largest island — a flat central plain around Manila and Pampanga, the Cordillera and Sierra Madre mountain ranges to the north and east, and active volcanoes such as Mayon and Taal.
nature.climate_signature: Hot and humid tropical, with a marked wet and dry season and frequent typhoons — cooler and pine-covered in the northern highlands around Baguio.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Metro Manila also has heavy bus, UV Express van and motorbike traffic.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: The densest and most complete coverage in the Philippines, concentrated in and around Metro Manila and along Luzon's main highways.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national plate and bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Luzon's Manila ladder-style pole-tops, Bicol's three-black-stripe white guardrails and northern Cordillera rice terraces are Luzon-specific; Mindanao's Zamboanga peninsula has square metal mesh poles, and mosques and Islamic architecture appear in the south.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar tropical rice-paddy landscape, concrete shophouse towns and motorbike traffic, both drive on the right
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Vietnamese signage uses Latin script with heavy diacritics, while Luzon signage is plain English/Tagalog; jeepneys, tricycles and Spanish-colonial churches are strong Philippines tells.
